To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
limiting nutrients to beef cows during late gestation does not influence ovarian follicle numbers of their daughters, nor does it impact their age at puberty or fertility.

limiting nutrient intake during the last two trimesters of gestation in mature beef cows does not decrease antral follicular numbers in their daughters or affect their reproductive performance, but increasing maternal nutrient intake in the last trimester improves fertility of their daughters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how maternal nutrition during the second and/or third trimesters of gestation affects ovarian follicle numbers and reproductive performance of female offspring.

the effects of maternal nutrient intake during late-gestation on ovarian reserve and fertility of female offspring.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the nutritional status of beef cow dams during the second and/or third trimester does not influence the reproductive performance of their daughters, but that increasing the nutritional status of dams during the third trimesters can improve first service conception rates.
limiting nutrients to pregnant beef cows during the third trimesters has the potential to increase the fertility of daughters.
limiting nutrient intake to beef cows during the third trimesters does not negatively impact reproductive performance of daughters, but may positively impact their fertility as first calf heifers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fluctuating nutrient intake to mature cows across the production cycles is an effective method to decrease input costs and does not negatively influence the fertility of daughters.
the ovarian follicle reserve of beef cattle does not appear to be influenced by the nutrient status of the dam during the second and/or third trimesters.
limiting nutrient intake during the last trimester in beef cows does not affect the reproductive potential of daughters.
The main takeaway from our work is that

limiting nutrient intake to mature cows during the third trimesters of gestation does not have negative impacts on their female offspring, which is important information to consider for cow/calf producers that may be interested in using fluctuating nutrient intake to decrease feed costs.
we have shown that limiting nutrients to beef cows during late gestation does not have a negative impact on the reproductive potential of their daughters.
limiting nutrients to cows during the third trimesters of pregnancy does not have a detrimental effect on their daughters’ reproductive performance.
